finding.message: Detected possible user input going into a `path.join` or `path.resolve` function. This could possibly lead to a path traversal vulnerability,  where the attacker can access arbitrary files stored in the file system. Instead, be sure to sanitize or validate user input first.

reason: writeFiles() loops over STATIC_FILES and calls fs.writeFileSync(path.join(destPath, file), ...) at line 177. The `file` argument is always a fixed literal map key (activity-stream.html, -debug, -noscripts), not external data. destPath comes from main() as path.join(path.resolve(__dirname, options.addonPath), 'prerendered'); options.addonPath is the only 'tainted' value, an optional --addon-path CLI flag defaulting to '..'. This file is a Node build/dev script run only via `node ./bin/render-activity-stream-html.js` from npm/yamscripts, never shipped or executed in the browser. Semgrep flags the argv-derived path.join generically; the only actor who can control it is a developer already running the build, so there is no runtime or attacker-reachable traversal.

finding.message: Depending on the context, user control data in `Object.assign` can cause web response to include data that it should not have or can lead to a mass assignment vulnerability.

reason: addBuiltInSection parses the `${feed}.options` pref string with JSON.parse (line 165) and passes the result into the built-in section generator (line 171), then shallow-clones the generated section and its `pref` object with Object.assign (lines 172-174), sets `section.pref.feed`/`section.options`, and registers it via addSection. Semgrep flags the Object.assign on line 172 because its source, `defaultSection`, derives from pref-supplied (user-controlled) JSON; the rule warns that bulk copying untrusted data can cause mass assignment. In practice the generator only reads `options.provider_icon`, so no arbitrary keys are merged.

finding.message: Depending on the context, user control data in `Object.assign` can cause web response to include data that it should not have or can lead to a mass assignment vulnerability.

reason: The finding is a false positive: Object.assign copies a locally constructed, code-owned defaultSection into a fresh object; the only pref-controlled data is stored on section.options and is never merged into the section. Replacing Object.assign with spread only avoids the semgrep pattern, and the new plain-object check adds unrelated behaviour: JSON values like 'null', '[]' or '3' now log the misleading 'Problem parsing options pref' and fall back to {}, where previously they reached the generator (null then failed later at options.provider_icon). Reject and treat the rule hit as a false positive; no rewrite is warranted.
